title: Jump into a hole through the Earth and you come out 42 minutes later

beats.say: Dig a hole straight through the Earth and jump in. 42 minutes later, you arrive on the other side.
beats.speak: Dig a hole straight through the Earth and jump in. Forty two minutes later, you arrive on the other side.

head: GRAVITY PULLS YOU
TO THE CENTRE.
beats.say: Pump all the air out, so nothing slows you. Gravity pulls you toward the centre the whole way down, so you keep speeding up.

head: AT THE CENTRE:
28,475 KM/H.
beats.say: At the centre you're doing 7.91 kilometres per second. That's 28,475 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: At the centre you're doing seven point nine one kilometres per second. That's twenty eight thousand four hundred and seventy five kilometres an hour.

head: THEN GRAVITY
PULLS YOU BACK.
beats.say: Past the centre, gravity pulls backwards. You slow down, stop right at the far side, and fall back. A round trip takes 84.35 minutes. Forever.
beats.speak: Past the centre, gravity pulls backwards. You slow down, stop right at the far side, and fall back. A round trip takes eighty four point three five minutes. Forever.

head: ANY STRAIGHT
TUNNEL.
beats.say: Here's the weird part. A straight tunnel between any two cities takes the same 42 minutes. A shorter tunnel just has a gentler slope.
beats.speak: Here's the weird part. A straight tunnel between any two cities takes the same forty two minutes. A shorter tunnel just has a gentler slope.

head: THE MOON:
SMALLER, YET SLOWER.
beats.say: Do it on the Moon. It's much smaller, but the trip takes longer: 54.17 minutes, because the Moon is far less dense than Earth.
beats.speak: Do it on the Moon. It's much smaller, but the trip takes longer: fifty four point one seven minutes, because the Moon is far less dense than Earth.

head: THE REAL EARTH
IS FASTER.
beats.say: The real Earth packs most of its mass in a heavy core. In 2015, a McGill student used seismic data to redo the sum: 38 minutes and 11 seconds.
beats.speak: The real Earth packs most of its mass in a heavy core. In two thousand and fifteen, a McGill student used seismic data to redo the sum: thirty eight minutes and eleven seconds.

head: HOW DEEP
HAVE WE DUG?
beats.say: The deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola borehole in Russia, reached 12,261 metres. That's 0.19% of the way to the centre.
beats.speak: The deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola borehole in Russia, reached twelve thousand two hundred and sixty one metres. That's zero point one nine percent of the way to the centre.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

caption: What if you dug a hole straight through the Earth and jumped in? With the air pumped out and Earth treated as a ball of even density, you fall for 42 minutes and arrive at the far side just as you stop. At the centre you are doing 7.91 km/s, 28,475 km/h. Then you fall back: one round trip every 84.35 minutes, forever. Strangely, a straight tunnel between any two points takes the same 42 minutes. On the Moon the trip takes longer, 54.17 minutes, because the Moon is far less dense. The real Earth is denser toward its core, and a 2015 study using seismic data (Alexander Klotz, McGill, American Journal of Physics) got 38 minutes and 11 seconds. The deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola borehole, reached 12,261 m: 0.19% of the way to the centre.
notes: NASA NSSDC Moon fact sheet (Moon and Earth columns): Earth GM 0.39860 x10^6 km3/s2, mean radius 6371.0 km; Moon GM 0.00490 x10^6 km3/s2, mean radius 1737.4 km. Phys.org (Mar 2015): Alexander Klotz, McGill University, American Journal of Physics 83, 231 (2015), used seismic data on Earth's varying density and got 38 minutes and 11 seconds instead of the accepted 42 minutes. arXiv 2411.18758 (The Gravity Tunnel Superhighway): in a uniform-density Earth any two points joined by a straight tunnel are traversed in the same 42 minutes (Cooper 1966). Guinness World Records: the Kola borehole near Zapolyarny, Russia, reached 12,261 m by 1983. Physics: inside a uniform ball gravity grows linearly with distance from the centre, so the fall is simple harmonic motion; one way time = pi*sqrt(R^3/GM), top speed = sqrt(GM/R). No air, no rotation, no heat: a thought experiment. Kola percentage uses the mean radius as the distance to the centre. The animation is not real time and the Moon is not drawn to scale.
